subject: Biology
title: Plant Hormones
description: A short lesson to help you apply Plant Hormones.

hook.text: Plants can't move toward sunlight. Instead, they grow toward it—guided by chemical hormones.

buildup.text: Auxin is a hormone that controls cell elongation. It makes stems bend toward light.

discovery.text: Gibberellins trigger seed germination and stem growth. Ethylene ripens fruit.

twist.text: One rotten apple really does spoil the bunch—it releases ethylene gas that ripens nearby fruit.

climax.text: Plants use hormones to coordinate growth, defense, flowering, and response to stress.

punchline.text: Plants can't run, so they grow their way out of trouble.

quiz.question: Which hormone makes plant stems bend toward light?

details.summary: Plant hormones coordinate growth, development, and responses to the environment. Auxin controls directional growth, cytokinins promote cell division, gibberellins drive stem elongation and germination, abscisic acid triggers dormancy, and ethylene controls fruit ripening and leaf drop.
details.whyItMatters: Plant hormones are used in agriculture to control ripening, rooting, weed killing, and fruit development. Understanding their action improves crop production and explains how plants coordinate complex behaviors without a nervous system.
takeaways: Auxin causes cells to elongate on the shaded side, bending stems toward light
Ethylene gas triggers coordinated fruit ripening and is used commercially
Abscisic acid closes stomata during drought to conserve water

faq.question: How does one banana ripen others in a bowl?
faq.answer: Ripening bananas release ethylene gas. Nearby fruits detect this ethylene and accelerate their own ripening. This positive feedback ensures fruits ripen together, which in nature attracts seed-dispersing animals to a concentrated reward. Commercially, ethylene is used to ripen stored fruit.

faq.question: How do herbicides like 2,4-D kill weeds?
faq.answer: 2,4-D mimics auxin but is not broken down by the plant. It causes uncontrolled, lethal growth in broadleaf weeds while grasses are unaffected due to different auxin metabolism. This selective action makes it one of the most widely used herbicides worldwide.
